liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tennessee Jed** (2 reviews): Reviewer can't recall a better version; Keith pounds the keys and the band plays very tightly; Reviewer calls it excellent, following a very good Sugaree that stays within the typical length range [10][17]
- **Saint Stephen** (2 reviews): Rocking version with an upbeat, long jam, arriving just as Playing In The Band got syrupy; followed by a short Wheel; Reviewer loves the intro, with Garcia's spacey guitar tone and effects, plus strong crowd reaction [11][20]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Opens the show in rollicking fashion [17]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer notes Scarlet Begonias was played between Looks Like Rain and Lazy Lightning, though missing from their copy [13]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Reviewer finds it strong [17]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Heart-wrenching lyrically; Keith dominates while Jerry weaves among his keys rather than overshadowing them [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-06-26.178703.mtx.seamons.ht31.flac1644** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1976-06-26.sbd.miller.95306.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 179 min; rated 4.31/5 by 13 [2]
- **gd1976-06-26.mtx.seamons.95355.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 179 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1976-06-26.165170.akg.weidner.wagner.miller.t-flac1644**: source not stated; 22 songs; 174 min [4]
- **gd76-06-26.aud.vernon.7340.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording described as a bit hollow but very crisp [12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says it was their first show and the first Chicago date after the band's return from retirement [9]
- The Auditorium felt intimate, opera-house-like, with good acoustics; the crowd was eager and energetic [9]
- Reviewer sat twelve rows back, center, at the Auditorium Theatre in downtown Chicago [12]
- The band had taken only one rest day in nine nights, on June 25 [18]
- Reviewer says 7/17/76 is stronger throughout and nearly unknown, while this tape circulated widely thanks to good quality [11]
- Reviewer ranks this Stella with the 6-15 and 7-18 versions from the same year as favorites [15]
- Reviewer says this opens a magical run at the Auditorium Theatre, following the good Tower Theatre shows [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-06-26.178703.mtx.seamons.ht31.flac1644**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) August… [1]. Also: Matrix built from a soundboard and an audience source; the earlier 2002 audience source was higher generation, thinner and channel-swapped; Earlier matrix lacked Scarlet Begonias and some tuning; edits trimmed tuning, removed dead air and clicks in Peggy-O and Playing [1]
- **gd1976-06-26.sbd.miller.95306.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Apogee Ensemble -> Peak -> AIFF [2]. Also: Unknown mics to master cassette, transferred via Apogee Ensemble; patch source for Tennessee Jed recorded with mics near the soundboard [2]
- **gd1976-06-26.mtx.seamons.95355.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [3]. Also: Soundboard to master cassette, transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [3]
- **gd1976-06-26.165170.akg.weidner.wagner.miller.t-flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Dave Weidner; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  March 14, 2022; source: AKG D200E > Cassette Master (Sony TC-153SD) > Cassette (TDK SA-C90/Dolby B) [4]. Also: Tape for Set II's Playing In The Band opening was supplied by Bob Wagner, converted from 24-bit/48k to 16/44.1 [4]
- **gd76-06-26.aud.vernon.7340.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerrybase: [Grateful Dead – 1976-06-26](https://jerrybase.com/events/19760626-01) [22]
